A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ITERGEN framework. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, algorithms, figures, tables and grammars, support comparison across additions, renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original Spider SQL-generation and DecodingTrust privacy experiments, plus recurrence-penalty and execution-feedback ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports SQL and privacy experiments, adds original Vega-Lite evaluation, and presents rejection-sampling comparisons and budget-sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 changes the reported recurrence multiplier from gamma to (1-gamma)^alpha, where alpha counts backtracking occurrences. Section 4.3 also introduces Vega-Lite-specific checks, including completing unordered channel objects before checking field/type compatibility. The core grammar navigation, symbol-position mapping and cache architecture remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds natural-language-to-Vega-Lite visualization generation using 814 NLV Corpus examples, substantially extending the evaluated task requirements beyond SQL and email privacy. The Spider and DecodingTrust coverage is retained; mentions of Python support and CRANE benchmarks do not establish additional evaluations by this work.

E2.justification: The privacy comparison expands beyond STANDARD generation to sampling, repetition-penalized sampling, contrastive search and diverse beam search within rejection-sampling comparisons (Table 5). v2 also adds whole-output rejection-sampling comparisons for SQL and Vega-Lite. The existing STANDARD, SYNCODE and SQL execution-feedback comparisons remain.

E3.justification: SQL evaluation expands from seven to nine model configurations, adding Llama-2-7b-chat-hf and Llama-3-8B. New protocols include stochastic pass@k comparisons, one-example prompting with exact-match and compiler-success metrics for Vega-Lite, and sweeps over 50–200 tokens and 10–30 iterations. These substantially extend the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 adds iteration/backtracking distributions, average call counts and limit-hit statistics, and sensitivity analyses for token limits and max_iter (Figures 4 and 6; Tables 7, 11 and 12). The original execution-feedback and error analyses are retained. The recurrence ablation retains its result values under the reversed gamma convention.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without seed information, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new pass@k comparisons change evaluation metrics and sampling procedures, but introduce no documented uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: SQL Table 1 revises accuracy, execution, token and timing values and adds two model blocks; for example, Qwen2.5-0.5B ITERGEN accuracy changes from 34.3% to 34.5%. v2 adds Vega-Lite, rejection-sampling and budget-analysis results. Privacy Table 2 and the execution-feedback table remain unchanged. The SQL updates cannot reliably be interpreted as same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: The recurrence-weight definition changes from gamma to (1-gamma)^alpha, explicitly introducing dependence on the number of backtracking occurrences. This is a limited mathematical revision beyond reversing the parameter convention. The formal grammar-symbol counts, forward/backward definitions and symbol-position mapping remain unchanged; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The introduction, contribution list and conclusion extend the demonstrated applications to Vega-Lite and add a claimed 17.8% accuracy improvement there. The central novelty claim about grammar-symbol-based bidirectional generation and the headline SQL/privacy claims are retained.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of token-budget and iteration tradeoffs, while removing v1's specific SQL speedup discussion and sliding-window-cache limitation without documenting a compatibility fix. The privacy exact-match caveat moves to Appendix A.3. A new claim of consistently beating Vega-Lite pass@k baselines conflicts with Table 6: SYNCODE reaches 37.66% at pass@5 versus ITERGEN's 36.01%.

D1.justification: v2 adds the Vega-Lite prompt and grammar, decoding settings for new comparisons, and an explicit 100-token cap for the existing main SQL evaluation; v1 does not specify that cap. It also adds a supplementary-code statement and project-resource link. The original hardware, software framework, SQL prompt and SQL/privacy grammars are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for Vega-Lite, the NLV Corpus and CRANE, positioning ITERGEN as a building block for CRANE. It removes the dedicated LMQL comparison paragraph and the sliding-window-cache citation, and changes the explanation for excluding SYNCHROMESH from unavailable code to problems running an unofficial implementation.

P1.justification: v2 expands the title, edits introductory and interface prose, renames Case Studies to Evaluation, and adds a reproducibility statement. Privacy methodology moves into the appendix, which groups SQL ablations, prompts and grammars under new headings. Most existing methodological prose and the main narrative sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with Vega-Lite and rejection-sampling tables, iteration statistics, budget-sensitivity tables and two scatterplots. SQL Table 1 gains model blocks. The privacy code figure moves to Appendix A.3 as Figure 5, while the architecture, parser and SQL-code illustrations remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The Vega-Lite evaluation tests broader applicability, while rejection-sampling controls and budget studies address gaps in v1's evidence for selective backtracking. Added reproduction details also help scrutiny. These benefits are tempered by stale SQL prose, Table 8 averages that disagree with Table 1, and the Vega-Lite superiority claim contradicted by Table 6. The net improvement is therefore limited.
